senses.definition: (uncountable, economics) Riches; a great amount of valuable assets or material possessions.
examples: Money talks, but true wealth whispers.

senses.definition: (countable) A great amount; an abundance or plenty.
examples: She brings a wealth of knowledge to the project.

quotes.text: There is a wealth of carved wood inside: from pulpit to pews, screens to lectern, and a large medieval chest made from a hollowed-out log of bog-oak with a massive lid.
quotes.reference: 1980, AA Book of British Villages, Drive Publications Ltd, page 269, about a church in Lower Peover:

quotes.text: Beyond its aim to bring patients the most effective treatments faster, the service is expected to generate a wealth of data on the interplay between DNA, health and lifestyles, which will become a powerful tool for research into cancer and other diseases.
quotes.reference: 2018 July 3, Ian Sample, “Routine DNA tests will put NHS at the 'forefront of medicine'”, in The Guardian:

quotes.text: I once did lend my body for his wealth, / Which, but for him that had your husband's ring, / Had quite miscarried: […]

quotes.text: Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth.
